column1: # tier-models.tsv — per-tier GATEWAY model FAILOVER CHAIN for the OFF-CLAUDE droid executor.
# COST IS A HEAVY WEIGHT (operator directive, 2026-08-01 — do not silently undo)
# Verbatim: "model expense should be a very heavy weight to them. If we have an option of a
# model that will do equally good work that is cheaper, the cheaper model should be used."
# And: "GPT models are way TOO expensive to run in any provider. We need to be VERY careful
# about sending work to expensive providers unless really required."
# RULES FOR EDITING THE CHAINS BELOW:
#   1. Order each chain CHEAPEST-CAPABLE FIRST. The first leg that can do the work well wins;
#      a costlier leg is a FAILOVER, never a default.
#   2. Adding an expensive leg requires a stated reason that the cheap legs demonstrably cannot
#      do the work — not a hunch, and not "for headroom".
#   3. REMOVED 2026-08-01 under this directive: `gpt-5.4-mini` (was strong, last leg) and
#      `gpt-5.4-nano` (was economy, last leg). Do NOT re-add an OpenAI GPT leg without an
#      explicit operator decision.
#   4. This is the same principle as the product's north-star router (need -> cheapest-capable
#      -> hold -> re-admit); the fleet's own dispatch must not violate what the product preaches.
# POOL DEPTH CAVEAT: dropping those legs leaves strong=3 and economy=2. If a chain empties,
# the fix is to add a CHEAP verified leg, never to re-add an expensive one.
# TIER AXIS (EVAL-TIER-CANON / review F-tier fix): the three tier names below
# (frontier | strong | economy) are the COST-BAND tiers — how expensive a model
# is, defined OBJECTIVELY by $/Mtok thresholds in fleet/state/TIER-CANON.md.
# TIER-CANON.md is the single source of truth for what each tier name MEANS;
# this file is the machine-consumed per-tier failover CHAIN (fleet-droid.sh
# parses it directly) — the tier DEFINITION lives there, the CHAIN lives here.
# The two are deliberately split: the cost-band rule is stable, the per-tier
# failover chain contents below are PROVISIONAL + operator-gated (see memory:
# charon-no-workhorse-finalized) and can be reordered without touching the
# cost-band definition, and vice versa.
# Do NOT confuse the cost-band tiers here with the separate CEILING-GRADE band
# (Frontier/Strong/Capable/Basic/No-Tier — an OUTPUT of
# EVAL-PIPELINE-CONSOLIDATE/F9's ramp, defined in
# fleet/benchmark/lib/tier_chart.py:23-28 TIER_LADDER). Same words, different
# axis — see TIER-CANON.md's disambiguation table. Cost band is an INPUT
# (price); ceiling grade is a MEASUREMENT (capability).
# For the deduped model-candidate roster (cost/funding/Path-C status) and the live provider list,
# see fleet/state/CG-MODEL-CANDIDATES.md + fleet/state/CG-PROVIDERS.md. This file stays the
# machine-consumed data source (fleet-droid.sh parses it directly) — edit it for real chain
# changes; the two CG- docs are the human-facing reference, not the other way around.
# Consumed by fleet/fleet-droid.sh to turn a tier arg into the ordered list of gateway model ids
# it hands the swappable work client ($CHARON_AGENT_CMD -> charon-run.sh). Each id is used as
# `charon/<id>` against the Charon gateway (4-LOM, http://10.0.1.60:8080), which itself fails over
# across PROVIDERS for one id; the chain here adds failover across MODELS when one is exhausted.
# These are NON-CLAUDE gateway models — the droid's WORK runs off Claude. (The MANAGER stays on
# Claude; only the droid work-execution step is off-Claude.)
# WHY A DATA FILE: `charon tier resolve` has NO non-anthropic executor and config has NO
# tier->gateway-model map (tier members are haiku/sonnet/opus only). So the per-tier gateway chain
# lives here — swap models by editing this file, ZERO code edits.
# PROVISIONAL — PENDING OPERATOR DECISION. NO workhorse-per-tier is finalized. The ids below are a
# provisional default drawn from cheap, gateway-proven models (seen live in the exhaustion ledger /
# model-scorecard); they are NOT a "chosen" workhorse. Model selection is pending real-code +
# benchmark testing (see memory: charon-no-workhorse-finalized). Reorder / replace freely.
# FORMAT: <canonical-tier> <ONE TAB> comma,separated,failover,chain   (cheapest-capable first)
# Exactly ONE tab between the two columns. Canonical tiers: frontier | strong | economy (the
# COST-BAND tiers — see fleet/state/TIER-CANON.md for the $/Mtok rule that DEFINES them).
# Legacy aliases (high/opus, med/sonnet, low/haiku) are normalized to these by fleet-droid.sh
# before lookup (alias fold lives in src/charon/config/tiers.py:_LEGACY_ALIASES).
# REVISED 2026-07-12 (LIGHT-MODELS-EVAL.md): spread economy/strong load OFF the frontier
# default deepseek-v4-pro. pro now lives ONLY in frontier (hard money-path work like F29);
# strong/economy are free-first onto flash-class coders with a paid deepseek-v4-flash leg
# ($0.077/$0.154) as the reliable backstop behind every free leg. All active ids verified
# reachable on gateway build 319658f. NanoGPT weekly cap is LIVE — keep a paid leg behind
# any -free/-ng leg. Base pool ids used so the gateway does its own provider failover.
frontier
strong
economy
